text:
Leah: quick flag — compact diff for eval runs makes the per-result CTA a kebab only. users are used to a persistent approve action. screenshot: https://figma.redwood/mock1 :eyes:
Jorge: we originally hid it to reduce clutter, but agree this hurts discoverability. keyboard flow goes to result > kebab > approve which is 3 steps. not great for a11y.
Aisha: suggestion: add a small top-level action when multiple items are selected: "Approve selected". keeps density low but gives a clear affordance. copy idea: "Approve selected" / "Approve checked" — prefer the first.
Mike: accessibility nits — current CTA contrast is ~2.7:1 on our token. needs 3:1+ for large text and 4.5:1 for normal. i can swap to token `--redwood-action-500` and run contrast check.
Mike: snippet:```css
.btn-approve {
  background: var(--redwood-action-500);
  color: #ffffff;
}
```
Leah: keyboard shortcut idea: allow `a` to approve focused items and `Shift+A` for bulk approve when multiple selected. Also toast copy: "Approved 3 prompts — changes saved to prompt set" with Undo.
DesignBot: automated accessibility scan: contrast fail on `.compact .result-meta` (text #6b7280 on #ffffff = 2.3:1). recommend bump to `#374151` or increase font weight.
Jorge: also noticed regression-diff timeline: compact view hides per-test headers which makes it hard to know which prompt the diff belongs to when scanning. propose collapsible headers that default collapsed in compact.
Aisha: we should extract the copy to i18n keys now: `evals.approve_selected`, `evals.toast.approved_set`. avoids late translation churn.
Leah: can someone mock two variants (inline CTA vs top-level batch CTA + collapsed headers) in Figma? i'll collect feedback in tomorrow's design sync. target: pick direction by EOD so eng can scope for next sprint. :clock3:
Mike: i'll update color tokens and push a quick prototype. pinging eng-frontend after mock. :thumbsup: 
Aisha: i'll review the strings and accessibility notes today.
Leah: awesome, thanks team — tagging this for design-review tomorrow. :raised_hands:
